main_body: A stilt hut. A large plank-panel roof (rows 1-20) sits over a wall with a door and a window (rows 22-35), a porch beam at row 35, and thin stilts below.
top_band: Only a 1-row light edge (#d9a566, row 1) under the outline. Below it rows 2-20 are the same mid-brown family as the plank face (L 98 down to 73), with no separate top surface.
evidence: The roof is a flat front panel of vertical planks, with only a 1-row highlight along the ridge. It shows no top slope, and no step of 25 L or more separates a top band from the face. The wall below is also painted flat. The door and window are drawn with dark outlines but are not convincingly inset. The porch beam at rows 35-36 is a thin 1-2 row band. The whole drawing reads as a front elevation with a thin rim, so it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against 66-185 colours and 11-18 per tile in the references. The planks are separated by dark brown, tinted lines (0% neutral edge pixels), but the shading is a basic brown ramp with no per-plank grain or speckle. The roof has no tile or shingle texture or per-element highlights, so it looks flatter and simpler than the Beodeul houses. There are no 5x5 flat blocks, but the density is far below the references.
